Looking for impact sounds…

1. Confirm the frames

Find racket contact and the ball’s first bounce. Audio suggestions are starting points, not confirmed measurements.

Racket contactNot confirmed
First bounceNot confirmed

Height of the ball when it meets the racket. 2.7 m is a starting assumption; adjust if known.

2. Set the flight positions

Choose a marker, then tap the court diagram where the server and first bounce were. No full-court video is needed.

Near baseline: y = 0. Far service line: y = 18.285 m. x = 0 is the center line.

3. Review the estimate

Mark at least four known points in the paused video. Use any visible portion, spread across two or more court lines. Choose exact painted intersections or baseline center ticks.

Use one paused frame for all anchors. If the camera angle changes, calibrate that shot again or use the diagram method.

Use a larger value when landing position is uncertain. The range varies both marked positions by this amount, timing by one frame, and height by 0.4 m.

Confirm both frames and positions to calculate a speed.

The estimate updates as you edit. Diagram placement gives a rough estimate; calibration improves court distances but still depends on your clicks.

GIVE IT A CLEAR VIEW

A better clip.
A better estimate.

01

Keep the camera still

A fixed camera makes calibration reusable. For changing angles, use the diagram method or calibrate each shot separately.

02

Partial court is fine

Portrait clips work with manual positions. For calibration, identify four visible court points across at least two lines.

03

Prefer 60 fps

Use the original video with sound. 30 fps and variable-rate phone recordings also work. Use real-time footage; avoid slow-motion exports.

What does this estimate measure?+

The app divides the straight-line distance from contact to first bounce by video flight time, approximating average flight speed. Court-diagram positions are your estimates; calibrated positions come from four or more marked court points. The start position is the ground point beneath contact, not the airborne ball. Contact height is entered separately.

Audio transients suggest possible racket contacts so you can separate multiple shots. Practice bounces, voices, other courts, and echoes can produce false suggestions. Always confirm contact and bounce visually. Audio times are not used directly for speed, avoiding sound-travel delay in the measurement.

The displayed range is a sensitivity band for your stated position tolerance, one frame of timing variation, and 0.4 m of contact-height variation. It is not a validated confidence interval and does not cover every calibration or lens error. This measures neither spin nor radar speed at impact; accuracy has not been validated against radar.
